title: Bash file
body:
`.bashrc` (and `.bash_profile`), the startup files the [[Shell]] reads when you log in.
Anything you put in one runs every session, which is where your `alias` lines and your `PATH`
live.

```bash
PATH=$PATH:$HOME/BIN:.
alias go_to_dir="cd /users/dir/"
```

The `:.` on the end of `PATH` adds the current [[Directory]], which is what lets you run
`./a.out` as plain `a.out`. It is also why the course tells you to add it: without it the
shell looks everywhere except where you just compiled.

Editing it is a [[EMACS]] job, and changes take effect at the next login or after
`source ~/.bashrc`.

More generally a bash *script* is a text file of shell commands, made runnable with
`chmod +x`. Same commands you type by hand, saved so you stop retyping them. See [[Workflow]].
